passages.text: A Psalm. A song for the dedication of the temple. Of David.
passages.sermon: David wrote this psalm.\r\nThis psalm is a song.\r\nPeople sang this song at the dedication of the temple.

passages.text: I will exalt You, O LORD, for You have lifted me up and have not allowed my foes to rejoice over me.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
David sang this song for the dedication of the temple.
David speaks to the LORD.
David says, “I will exalt You, O LORD.”
David says, “You have lifted me up.”
David says, “You did not let my enemies rejoice over me.”
passages.original: מִזְמ֡וֹר שִׁיר־ חֲנֻכַּ֖ת הַבַּ֣יִת לְדָוִֽד׃ אֲרוֹמִמְךָ֣ יְ֭הוָה כִּ֣י דִלִּיתָ֑נִי וְלֹא־ שִׂמַּ֖חְתָּ אֹיְבַ֣י לִֽי׃

passages.text: O LORD my God, I cried to You for help, and You healed me.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm for the dedication of the temple.
David speaks to the LORD, his God.
David cried out to the LORD for help.
The LORD healed David.

passages.text: O LORD, You pulled me up from Sheol; You spared me from descending into the Pit.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is my God.
The LORD pulled me up from Sheol.
Sheol is the place of the dead.
The LORD saved my life.
The LORD kept me from going down into the Pit.
The Pit is a place of destruction and death.
The LORD rescued me from death.
passages.original: יְֽהוָ֗ה הֶֽעֱלִ֣יתָ מִן־ שְׁא֣וֹל נַפְשִׁ֑י חִ֝יִּיתַ֗נִי מִיּוֹרְדֵי בֽוֹר׃

passages.text: Sing to the LORD, O you His saints, and praise His holy name.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD.
God is holy.
God has saints.
Saints are people who belong to God.
Saints, sing to the LORD.
Saints, praise the holy name of the LORD.
passages.original: זַמְּר֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה חֲסִידָ֑יו וְ֝הוֹד֗וּ לְזֵ֣כֶר קָדְשֽׁוֹ׃

passages.text: For His anger is fleeting, but His favor lasts a lifetime. Weeping may stay the night, but joy comes in the morning.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is merciful.
His anger does not last long.
His anger is brief.
His favor lasts for a lifetime.
We may cry at night.
Weeping may remain through the evening.
Joy comes in the morning.
God brings joy after sorrow.
passages.original: כִּ֤י רֶ֨גַע׀ בְּאַפּוֹ֮ חַיִּ֪ים בִּרְצ֫וֹנ֥וֹ בָּ֭עֶרֶב יָלִ֥ין בֶּ֗כִי וְלַבֹּ֥קֶר רִנָּֽה׃

passages.text: In prosperity I said, “I will never be shaken.”
passages.sermon: I felt secure and at peace.\r\nI enjoyed prosperity.\r\nI said, “I will never be shaken.”
passages.original: וַ֭אֲנִי אָמַ֣רְתִּי בְשַׁלְוִ֑י בַּל־ אֶמּ֥וֹט לְעוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: O LORD, You favored me; You made my mountain stand strong. When You hid Your face, I was dismayed.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD showed me favor.
The LORD made me strong and secure.
The LORD gave me stability, like a strong mountain.
When the LORD hid His face from me, I became afraid.
When I lost His favor, I felt dismayed.
passages.original: יְֽהוָ֗ה בִּרְצוֹנְךָ֮ הֶעֱמַ֪דְתָּה לְֽהַרְרִ֫י עֹ֥ז הִסְתַּ֥רְתָּ פָנֶ֗יךָ הָיִ֥יתִי נִבְהָֽל׃

passages.text: To You, O LORD, I called, and I begged my Lord for mercy: “What gain is there in my bloodshed, in my descent to the Pit? Will the dust praise You? Will it proclaim Your faithfulness?
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
David was in distress.
David called out to the LORD.
David begged the Lord for mercy.
David said, “What benefit is there if I die?
What gain is there if I go down to the grave?
Will the dust praise You, God?
Will the dust speak of Your faithfulness?”
passages.original: אֵלֶ֣יךָ יְהוָ֣ה אֶקְרָ֑א וְאֶל־ אֲ֝דֹנָ֗י אֶתְחַנָּֽן׃ מַה־ בֶּ֥צַע בְּדָמִי֮ בְּרִדְתִּ֪י אֶ֫ל־ שָׁ֥חַת הֲיוֹדְךָ֥ עָפָ֑ר הֲיַגִּ֥יד אֲמִתֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: Hear me, O LORD, and have mercy; O LORD, be my helper.”
passages.sermon:
The speaker is David.  
David prays to the LORD.  
David says, "Hear me, O LORD."  
David asks, "Have mercy on me."  
David says, "O LORD, be my helper."
passages.original: שְׁמַע־ יְהוָ֥ה וְחָנֵּ֑נִי יְ֝הוָה הֱ‍ֽיֵה־ עֹזֵ֥ר לִֽי׃

passages.text: You turned my mourning into dancing; You peeled off my sackcloth and clothed me with joy, that my heart may sing Your praises and not be silent. O LORD my God, I will give thanks forever.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
David speaks to the LORD, his God.
You, LORD, changed my mourning into dancing.
You removed my sackcloth from me.
You dressed me with joy.
You did this so I would sing your praise.
You did this so I would not be silent.
LORD, my God, I will thank you forever.
passages.original: הָפַ֣כְתָּ מִסְפְּדִי֮ לְמָח֪וֹל לִ֥י פִּתַּ֥חְתָּ שַׂקִּ֑י וַֽתְּאַזְּרֵ֥נִי שִׂמְחָֽה׃ לְמַ֤עַן׀ יְזַמֶּרְךָ֣ כָ֭בוֹד וְלֹ֣א יִדֹּ֑ם יְהוָ֥ה אֱ֝לֹהַ֗י לְעוֹלָ֥ם אוֹדֶֽךָּ׃
